Game Day

FINAL – Kings 3, Bruins 0 – Zuccarello, Kuemper, Laviolette

By Zach Dooley
10 hours ago
123 Comments
Share This Article
Share This Article
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 8:52
Instaread

The LA Kings started off the roadtrip with a 3-0 victory over the Boston Bruins on Tuesday evening at TD Garden.

Inside the final stages of the first period, Kings forward Mats Zuccarello got the visitors on the board. Defenseman Erik Gustafsson started the play by gaining the offensive blue line off the rush wish possession. After Gustafsson’s shot was blocked, Zuccarello picked up the rebound in the left-hand circle and beat Boston goaltender Michael DiPietro clean with a wrist shot for his second goal in as many games and a 1-0 lead through 20 minutes.

After a strong second period offensively, the Kings doubled their advantage as the fourth line got in on the scoring. Forward Scott Laughton intercepted a pass along the wall deep in the offensive zone. He collected the puck onto his forehand and fired hard towards the top of the crease, deflecting off of forward Andre Lee and in for his second goal of the season and a two-goal advantage for the Kings.

Late in the third period, Gustafsson took a pass from goaltender Darcy Kuemper and picked the empty net, sealing the 3-0 victory with a multi-point game.

Hear from Zuccarello, Kuemper and Head Coach Peter Laviolette after tonight’s game.

Mats Zuccarello

Darcy Kuemper
On his takeaways from tonight’s win
It was nice for us to get back on the road here. We thought we built a lot on the last roadtrip, so unfortunately we’re disappointed with the homestand, but now we’re back on the road where we’ve been feeling pretty comfortable. So, nice to start off with a win.

On if he was just feeling dialed in tonight
The guys were doing a great job in front of me and I felt like I was able to see every shot. When we’re boxing out like that, it makes the goalie’s job a lot easier. I thought we did a great job in front of our net.

On a huge kill late in the game
The killers, everyone that was on the ice, was doing a great job. Our stand was awesome and we didn’t really let them set up at all. That can really kill the other team’s momentum and build momentum for us. After we got that kill, I think everyone felt pretty confident that we’re going to get the win.

On his penalty-shot save in the third period
Yeah, I was just trying to be as big as I could. Obviously, he’s a great shooter, so I wanted to take away as much net as I could and I got a piece of it.

Peter Laviolette
On his takeaways from tonight’s victory
Really good. I thought we competed really hard the whole night. They pushed, I thought, hard at the beginning, they pushed hard at the end, I thought we responded well to both. I thought we did a really good job right in front of Darcy. Darcy made some really big saves in there, a couple really big ones on the penalty kill in the second period, a couple really big ones in the third period, obviously the penalty shot, that could’ve make it 2-1 and change the complexion of the game. I thought he was really good, but overall, I thought our guys just competed really hard, really well the entire night.

On finding that second goal after a good stretch of play
Yeah, it’s been hard to get that next one, so it was good. The first six minutes, they had some shots, I think they had one good chance at missed the net, but I just thought it was a really fast period. We didn’t get anything offensively until the end of the period, but I do think just answering the bell in the first eight to 10 minutes and being ready to compete and ready to play [was important]. Like I said, I thought they pushed right away at the beginning of the game, so I thought it was a good response. Then, the last eight minutes of the first and the second period I really liked our game I thought we picked it up and attacked.

On Darcy Kuemper’s performance tonight and the confidence it gave the group
I mean, I thought Kuemps was great. We haven’t been getting wins. It hasn’t all been bad, we just haven’t been winning games, but you need that confidence with the win to build off of and move on to the next city and get another one. So, that’s the objective right now is to just get out of here and go to the next one and find the next win.

On the message at the timeout and if he felt it resonated
You knew that they were going to come, you knew that they’re going to push and so they did. It was just, we had played a really good 40 minutes and I don’t think you wanted to play the next 17 minutes like we did the first three minutes of the third period. So, just to go back to the mindset of the first and the second period where we were skating, we were working, we were competing on the defensive side of things. I thought the guys settled it down for the next eight to 10 minutes and got a win.

Notes –
– Forward Mats Zuccarello (1-0=1) scored his second goal in as many appearances following his tally on Saturday against Calgary. The native of Oslo, Norway, has four points (2-2=4) in his last three outings against Boston, dating back to March 2, 2025, as a member of the Minnesota Wild.
– Per NHL PR, Zuccarello became the fourth player to score in consecutive games for the Kings at age 39 or older, following Jarome Iginla (3 GP in 2016-17), Luc Robitaille (3 GP & 2 GP in 2005-06) and Corey Perry (3x: 2 GP in 2025-26)
– Forward Andre Lee (1-0=1) scored his second goal of the season, his first career point against the Boston Bruins––the third member of the Original Six against whom he has recorded a point (1 A, Oct. 27, 2026, at CHI; 1 A, Oct. 16, 2024, at TOR). Lee played his collegiate hockey near TD Garden, scoring 64 points (31-33=64) in 87 NCAA contests for the University of Massachusetts Lowell River Hawks from 2019-22.
– Defenseman Erik Gustafsson (1-1=2) returned to the Kings’ lineup tonight and found the scoresheet in his third consecutive game (1-4=5), dating back to his multi-assist effort on Nov. 4 against San Jose. The Nynashamn, Sweden, native recorded his sixth assist of the season on Zuccarello’s opening tally before icing an empty-net goal of his own from behind the Kings’ goal-line, securing his second multi-point showing of the season.
– Defenseman Brandt Clarke (0-1=1) notched his 11th assist of the season to extend his point streak to a third game (0-3=3), dating back to Nov. 12 against the Islanders and he is now tied with forward Artemi Panarin (11 A) for the lead in assists among Kings skaters this season.
– The native of Nepean, Ontario, has found the scoresheet in both meetings with the Bruins this year (0-1=1; Oct. 17), part of his six points (1- 5=6) in seven career matchups with the club from the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.
– Forward Scott Laughton (0-1=1) collected his fourth assist of the season.
– Goaltender Darcy Kuemper (0-1=1) turned aside a penalty shot attempt by Boston’s Morgan Geekie, one of 29 saves he made to earn his 40th career shutout and first of the 2026-27 campaign. Kuemper’s 12 shutouts as a member of the LA Kings rank fifth in franchise history.
– Per NHL PR, Kuemper became the fifth active goaltender to record 40 career shutouts and the fastest to hit the mark among that cohort (501 GP), eclipsing Connor Hellebuyck (516 GP).
– Additionally, Kuemper picked up his second helper of the campaign on Gustafsson’s second goal of the year, becoming the second goaltender in the NHL to have multiple assists on the season. The native of Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, has recorded five assists in a Kings uniform, breaking a tie with Bob Janecyk (4 A), Mathieu Garon (4 A), and Félix Potvin (4 A) for sole possession of the fifth-most in franchise history. Kuemper is the third goaltender in Kings history to post an assist and record a shutout in the same game, joining Félix Potvin (March 29, 2001 vs. CBJ) and Mario Lessard (Nov. 24, 1982 vs. NJD) and is the first to do so on the road. All three games were won by a score of 3-0.

The Kings are scheduled to practice tomorrow in Toronto at 1 PM at Ford Performance Arena in Etobicoke, Ontario, in advance of Thursday’s game against the Maple Leafs.
